samples.summary: The new `columnWidths` count cap is bypassed by the live slides reader — the one path a collaborating client actually renders through.
samples.evidence: The change adds `bandTableColumnWidths` inside `bandElementNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:80) and applies it on the board store (`YorkieBoardStore.readElement` generic tail), the revision snapshot adapters (`bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`) and the backend PUT (`assertValidTableData`). The *live slides* store does not use `bandElementNumerics` at all: `YorkieSlidesStore.readElement` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:545) hands the table branch to `bandElementText` (line 528-543), which only walks `rows[].cells[].body.blocks` and never touches `data.columnWidths`; the group branch recurses back into the same `readElement`. So a peer writing a table element with a million-entry `columnWidths` still reaches the renderer unbanded, and `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:41,87,92` takes `nCols = data.columnWidths.length` and loops/allocates per (row, column) pair — the exact hang the cap was added to prevent, on the only surface where the deck is edited collaboratively.

samples.summary: `PUT /content` now 400s on a wrong-typed inline `fontSize` (and master `fontSize`/`lineHeight`) that the matching `GET` still returns verbatim, so GET → edit → PUT of an already-stored slides deck can no longer round-trip.
samples.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` now throws `BadRequestException` for a non-number `style.fontSize`, and `bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` (docs-content.controller.ts:623) throws for a non-number master `fontSize`/`lineHeight`. The slides GET arm is `readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot())` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:158) and `readSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:52-81) returns the stored JSON verbatim — it neither bands nor coerces. A slide body stored with `fontSize: "24"` (accepted by the *previous* version of this validator, or written straight to the root by any collaborator's `doc.update`) is therefore returned by GET and then rejected by PUT, breaking the CLI's `content get`→edit→`content set` flow for that document. The in-code claim beside the throw ("a `GET` → edit → `PUT` cannot be 400ed by it") holds for docs bodies, which pass a codec, but not for slides bodies, which do not. The same class of value is explicitly documented as reachable in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:91-99 (a stored string `listLevel`).

samples.summary: `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics` on a board snapshot writes into the shared `DEFAULT_MASTER` / `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` module singletons, which the band's contract says it never receives.
samples.evidence: `parseBoardSnapshot` now wraps `boardToSlidesDocument(...)` in `bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`, but `boardToSlidesDocument` inserts the module constants by reference: `const master = DEFAULT_MASTER;` and `const layout = BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(l => l.id === 'blank')` → `masters: [master], layouts: [layout]` (packages/board/src/model/board.ts:44-70). `bandMasterNumerics` → `bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics` then *assigns* `record.fontSize` / `record.lineHeight` on the shared `DEFAULT_MASTER` object (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:181-190), contradicting the module header's "every caller passes a plain JSON copy it just materialized … nothing else observing it". Today the written values are identical to the defaults so nothing observable changes, but the invariant other modules rely on (these constants are immutable and shared process-wide) is violated, and any future non-default value or `Object.freeze` turns it into cross-document corruption or a strict-mode TypeError in the revision preview.

samples.summary: `duplicateSlide` still copies elements and notes unbanded, committing a peer-poisoned body into a second stored slide — the writer class this change fixed everywhere else.
samples.evidence: The change bands the writers that commit values into the CRDT (`resolveMasterAndTheme`, `resolveLayout`, `cascadeMasterStyles`, and the backend `apply()` in slides.controller.ts) on the stated principle that "a reader's band can only hide it". `duplicateSlide` was not updated: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:855 reads `sourceNotes` with a bare `yorkieToPlain<Block[]>` and line 843-861 copies `sourceElements` verbatim into `r.slides.splice(...)`, so a poisoned `fontSize: 1e9` / `rowSpan` in the source slide is written a second time into the document rather than repaired. Readers still band, so nothing renders wrong — but the stored poison spreads, which is precisely what the write-side bands exist to stop.

samples.summary: The backend master band *deletes* `fontSize`/`lineHeight`, which `PlaceholderStyle` types as required and the slides-side twin substitutes a default for — the two bands on the same field disagree.
samples.evidence: `bandMasterPlaceholderStyles` does `if (banded === undefined) delete style[field]` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:632), so a PUT carrying `fontSize: 0` stores a master whose placeholder style has no `fontSize`. `PlaceholderStyle` declares both as required numbers (packages/slides/src/model/master.ts:4-10), and the slides-side band added by this same change deliberately substitutes `DEFAULT_MASTER`'s value instead of dropping — `record.fontSize = normalizeFontSize(...) ?? fallback.fontSize` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:186), with its own doc note that `undefined` would paint `NaNpx` in the empty-placeholder hint and seed an undefined size. Consumers that read the stored master without the frontend band (the v1 `GET /content` arm at docs-content.controller.ts:158, and any CLI/API client off it) now receive a master missing a field the published model says is always present.

finding.evidence: The change adds `bandTableColumnWidths` inside `bandElementNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:80) and applies it on the board store (`YorkieBoardStore.readElement` generic tail), the revision snapshot adapters (`bandSlidesDocumentNumerics`) and the backend PUT (`assertValidTableData`). verdict.reason: Verified independently. The new columnWidths count cap lives only in bandTableColumnWidths (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:72-77), reachable only via bandElementNumerics' table branch (band-numerics.ts:99-100). The board store routes through it (yorkie-board-store.ts:442), but YorkieSlidesStore.readElement does not: its generic tail calls this.bandElementText(el.type, data) (yorkie-slides-store.ts:638), and bandElementText (lines 528-543) walks only shape.text.blocks and table rows[].cells[].body.blocks — it never touches data.columnWidths. bandElementNumerics is not imported in yorkie-slides-store.ts at all (repo-wide grep shows references only in yorkie-board-store.ts, slides node.ts/index.ts, and tests). Table elements do reach that tail: readElement branches early only for 'text' (556), 'connector' (579) and 'group' (612); the group branch recurses into the same readElement (624), so a table nested in a group is equally unbanded. The sink is real and unguarded: table-renderer.ts:41 and :87-92 take nCols = columnWidths.length, allocate nCols+1 offsets, and loop per (row, column) pair at :96-113 and :115-120 regardless of cell existence. A full columnWidths grep over packages/slides/src and packages/frontend/src shows no other length clamp on the read/render path, and MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS appears only in band-numerics.ts, the docs codec, and the backend controller — so the local-write mutators (yorkie-slides-store.ts:2434-2442, 2625-2635) do not close the hole against a peer writing directly into the CRDT, which is the threat model band-numerics.ts:11-31 explicitly states. This is a new guard with a reachable bypass on the primary collaborative render path: blast-radius lane, blocking.

verdict.reason: All cited code is present as described. docs-content.controller.ts:1313-1321 throws BadRequestException for a present, non-number inline `style.fontSize`, and bandMasterPlaceholderStyles (610-636, throw at 623-627) does the same for master `fontSize`/`lineHeight`; it is called unconditionally from the slides body validator at 586-589. The matching GET arm (156-160) returns readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot()), and readSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:52-81) only unwraps JSON and defaults `meta` — it neither bands nor coerces, and writeSlidesRoot (93-110) stores the arrays verbatim, so the slides path has no codec to normalize wrong-typed numerics on read (unlike docs, whose codec coerces strings — packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts:101). The "wrong-typed numeric stored verbatim in a deck" class is explicitly documented as reachable in this repo at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:88-99, which says a stored string `listLevel` arrives at the exporter with that type precisely because slide bodies pass no codec. The CLI's set path sends the body verbatim (packages/cli/src/commands/content-write.ts:23,47), so nothing between GET and PUT repairs the value, and a stored deck holding a string fontSize can be read but no longer written back. No guard elsewhere makes the path unreachable; the behaviour is deliberately test-pinned (docs-content.validation.spec.ts:190-194, 231-243), which corroborates rather than refutes. The in-code claim at 1303-1311 that a GET→edit→PUT "cannot be 400ed by it" does not hold for the slides arm. Pre-existing similar rejections at assertValidBlockStyle:408-416 reduce novelty but not reality or impact.

finding.summary: `cascadeMasterStyles` reads the master's placeholder typography straight off the live CRDT, bypassing the new `bandMasterNumerics` guard, and commits the poisoned value into real blocks
finding.evidence: The change bands masters at the two readers it found — `read()` (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:485`) and `resolveMasterAndTheme()` (`:1322`), the latter with the explicit rationale "this is the reader that actually feeds `seedPlaceholderBlocks`: without it a poisoned master's `fontSize` is *committed* to the CRDT". But `updateMaster()` passes the **live, unbanded** master object (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:1082` `(r as { masters?: Master[] }).masters?.find(...)`) into `cascadeMasterStyles`, which at `:1144-1147` does `const style = yorkieToPlain<PlaceholderStyle>((master.placeholderStyles as Record<string, unknown>)[t]); if (style) data.blocks = clone(seedPlaceholderBlocks(style, theme));`. So any user who touches master typography on a deck whose `masters` a peer poisoned writes `fontSize: 1e9` / `lineHeight: 1e9` into every empty placeholder's stored `data.blocks` — exactly the outcome the `resolveMasterAndTheme` band and the new `keeps a poisoned master out of the blocks a layout change seeds` test exist to prevent. Fix belongs on the new code: band `master` (or `style`) before the seed at line 1147.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `cascadeMasterStyles` in the Yorkie store seeds blocks from an unbanded live-CRDT placeholder style (`if (style) data.blocks = clone(seedPlaceholderBlocks(style, theme))`). That code is not present. At packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:1151-1157 the style pulled off the live master is passed through `bandPlaceholderStyleNumerics(style, t)` before `seedPlaceholderBlocks`, with an in-place comment (lines 1145-1150) citing exactly the `updateMaster`-hands-us-the-unbanded-object scenario the reviewer describes. The helper is a real exported function (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:180-200, exported at packages/slides/src/index.ts:64, imported at yorkie-slides-store.ts:43) that clamps `fontSize`/`lineHeight` via the docs normalizers with DEFAULT_MASTER fallbacks. A test asserting the stored CRDT JSON (not `read()`) after `updateMaster` with `fontSize: 1e9` expects MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_LINE_HEIGHT: packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:1066-1099. The suggested fix is already the shipped code, so there is no bypassing site to block on.

finding.summary: `resolveLayout()` returns a layout unbanded, so `addSlide` / `applyLayout` copy a peer-poisoned layout placeholder body into a real slide element — the write-side twin of the `read()` layout band the diff added
finding.evidence: `read()` now bands layouts (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:470-472`) with the stated reason that placeholder specs carry the same codec-free `data.blocks` and "`seedPlaceholderBlocks` copies their typography into the real blocks a layout change materializes". The path that actually materializes them does not use `read()`: `resolveLayout()` (`:1344-1350`) does a bare `yorkieToPlain<Layout[]>(root.layouts)` with no `bandLayoutNumerics`, and its result feeds `addSlide` (`:746`, which clones `placeholder.data` verbatim for every non-text placeholder at `:782-786`, and falls back to `placeholderData.blocks` at `:768`) and `applyLayout` (`:1288` → `applyLayoutToSlide`, which pushes `clone(slot.spec)` wholesale at `packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:434,456-461` — only a *text* slot's `blocks` are replaced by the seed, so a poisoned `shape` placeholder's `data.text.blocks` rides through). The poisoned numerics are then committed to the Yorkie root for every viewer. Fix belongs on the new code: wrap `resolveLayout`'s result in `bandLayoutNumerics`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `resolveLayout()` returns the layout unbanded (bare `yorkieToPlain<Layout[]>(root.layouts)` with no `bandLayoutNumerics`), leaving `addSlide`/`applyLayout` as a write-side bypass of the `read()` layout band. That code is not present. `resolveLayout` at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:1355-1367 ends with `return layout ? bandLayoutNumerics(layout) : getLayout(layoutId);`, and its doc comment at :1361-1365 states the exact rationale the finding says is absent. `bandLayoutNumerics` is imported at :41 (exported at packages/slides/src/index.ts:62). Both alleged bypassing consumers consume the banded value: `addSlide` at :747 and `applyLayout` at :1299 -> `applyLayoutToSlide` at :1307; there is no other write-path read of `root.layouts` (the only other one is `read()` at :471-473, also banded). The shape-placeholder sub-case is covered too: `bandLayoutNumerics` (packages/slides/src/model/band-numerics.ts:127-136) walks `placeholders` and `staticElements` via `bandElementNumerics`, whose `shape` branch bands `data.text.blocks` at :92-98. A regression test for precisely this path exists at packages/frontend/tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:1101-1138 (hostile shape placeholder -> `addSlide` -> stored element clamped to MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_LINE_HEIGHT). The line numbers cited by the reviewer (:1344-1350) point at `resolveMasterAndTheme`'s fallback, not `resolveLayout`, indicating the finding was written against a different revision.
